proof.criterion: The architect skill states the lifecycle a merged close actually has, so an architect reading `child-closed` learns what happens to the implementer's pod.
proof.surface: The daemon's own source, read before the sentence was rewritten rather than after.
proof.observed: `if merged { except = claim.RoleImplementer }` and the `record.IssueSuspend` enqueued only `if !merged`. So a merged close queues no suspension at all: the implementer keeps its pod for the production check's first look, and the Sandbox goes only when a look reports `pending`. `skills/legion-architect/SKILL.md:417-421` now says that; the generated copy at `packages/claude-envoy/legion/skills/legion-architect/SKILL.md:418` carries it after `bun run build`, with `bun run check-dist` reporting `dist/ and legion/ match a fresh build`.
proof.negativeControl: `grep -rn "Sandbox deleted with its pod, since it still" packages/ skills/` is empty: the sentence this change wrote survives nowhere, the generated mirror included. Before the rebuild it appeared twice.

proof.criterion: The Stage 4b checkpoint that watches the suspension happen describes what the daemon deletes.
proof.surface: The harness's own comment at the point where a `pending` look ends the pod.
proof.observed: The clause said the daemon suspends the implementer's claim and the issue's Sandbox 'with its volume'. That Sandbox owns none: the disk is the pod's own ephemeral volume, so the deletion takes the pod and the disk with it. The comment says that now, and the harness parses.
proof.negativeControl: Not applicable: a comment with no executable behaviour. Its control is the code it describes — `issuePod.claimTemplates` returns nil and `diskSource` renders a generic ephemeral volume, both pinned by the sandbox suite, which is green at this head.

The round-5 census kept main's wording on purpose and the reviewer argued it back; I took the argument — a list of accepted values naming a refused one sends an operator who mistyped to a value that is refused again.

discoveredComplexity: A change can make a sentence false by correcting it. The edit that put 'the Sandbox deleted with its pod' into the architect skill was written from this change's own subject and not from the close it describes, and it replaced a half-wrong sentence with a differently-wrong one stated more confidently.

A scope rule that says 'do not flag unchanged code' excludes the whole class of text a change makes false without touching, which is the class this tree has filed on in nine of ten rounds. The replacement — text a change makes false in a file it owns — is what found all five of this round's.
